name: Endpoint Protection Platform
definition: Software on a managed endpoint that aims to prevent malware and unwanted code from installing or running, typically through signature, heuristic, and behavioural engines. It is the preventive layer that pairs with endpoint detection and response.

name: Endpoint Detection and Response
definition: Continuous recording of endpoint process, file, and network activity so that analysts can detect, investigate, and respond to suspicious behaviour on hosts. It keeps a queryable history rather than only blocking at the moment of execution.

name: Extended Detection and Response
definition: Correlation of detection signals across more than one domain, such as endpoint, identity, email, and network, into a single investigation and response workflow. It extends the endpoint detection model to additional telemetry sources.

name: Managed Detection and Response
definition: A service in which an external team operates detection and response tooling on a customer's behalf, monitoring telemetry and triaging or responding to alerts around the clock. The capability is delivered as a managed service rather than only as software.

name: Vulnerability Management
definition: Discovering assets, scanning them for known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, and tracking the findings through prioritisation and remediation. It is an ongoing cycle rather than a one-time scan.

name: Attack Surface Management
definition: Discovering an organisation's internet-facing assets from the outside, including unknown or forgotten ones, and monitoring them for exposure. It focuses on what an external attacker can see and reach.

frameworks.name: Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets

name: Security Information and Event Management
definition: Central collection, normalisation, and correlation of logs and events from across an environment so that activity can be searched, alerted on, and retained. It is the aggregation and detection layer a security operations centre queries.

name: Security Orchestration, Automation and Response
definition: Codifying response steps into playbooks that automate and orchestrate actions across tools, with case management for the analysts who run them. It aims to shorten and standardise how teams respond to alerts.

name: Email Security
definition: Inspecting inbound and outbound email to filter phishing, malware, and business-email-compromise attempts before or after delivery. It covers gateway and integrated (API-based) approaches to the email channel.

name: Network Detection and Response
definition: Analysing network traffic and flow records to detect suspicious behaviour that endpoint tooling may miss, and supporting investigation of it. It models normal network activity and flags deviations.

name: Next-Generation Firewall
definition: A network firewall that adds application awareness, user identity, and integrated threat inspection to traditional port and protocol filtering. It enforces policy at network boundaries and segments.

name: Security Service Edge
definition: Delivering web gateway, cloud access, and private-application access controls from the cloud so that policy follows users wherever they connect. It is the security half of the secure access service edge model.

name: Identity and Access Management
definition: Authenticating users and governing their access to applications through single sign-on, multi-factor authentication, and access policy. It is the control point for who may sign in and to what.

name: Privileged Access Management
definition: Securing, brokering, and recording the use of privileged and administrative accounts, often with credential vaulting, rotation, and session monitoring. It narrows and audits the most powerful access in an environment.

name: Identity Governance and Administration
definition: Managing the lifecycle of identities and entitlements, including provisioning, access reviews, and certification, so that access stays appropriate over time. It governs who should have access, not only who can sign in.

name: Application Security Testing
definition: Testing application code and its dependencies for security weaknesses, through static analysis, dynamic analysis, and software composition analysis. It aims to find flaws before or soon after software ships.

name: Crowdsourced Security Testing
definition: Coordinating external researchers to find and report vulnerabilities, through bug bounty programmes, vulnerability disclosure programmes, and researcher-driven testing. It draws on a community of testers rather than only internal staff.

name: Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform
definition: Combining cloud posture management, workload protection, and related cloud risk functions into one platform that covers applications from code to runtime in cloud environments. It consolidates several cloud security tools under one model.

frameworks.name: Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software

name: Operational Technology Security
definition: Discovering and monitoring industrial and operational-technology assets and their protocols, and detecting threats to them, usually with passive methods suited to fragile control systems. It applies security visibility to environments where availability and safety come first.

frameworks.name: Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets

name: Backup and Cyber Recovery
definition: Creating and protecting recoverable copies of data and systems, and restoring them after loss or attack, increasingly with immutable or isolated copies aimed at ransomware. It is the capability an organisation relies on to return to a trusted state.
